The idea is about the size of the day's move relative to its own open, so I'll start with the simplest form: the close-to-open ratio minus one, logged, which makes it unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0000 (t = -0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain ratio is essentially the day's return, which is fully absorbed by the reversal style — incremental IC is exactly 0.0000, so the raw size of the move carries no new information. Next I'll measure the same idea as a bounded ratio of the close to the open, so coins that close far above their open are ranked high within their own recent range rather than measured in absolute return units.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0277
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0074 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0128, 2023 -0.0074, 2024 -0.0046

Bounded range-normalized version is clearly negative and consistent across all three periods, so on this history coins closing far above their open tend to give some back. One more form worth checking: the same close-to-open ratio but measured over a few days rather than one day, which overlaps less with the daily return already removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0001 (t = 0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 -0.0001

The five-day average of the same ratio is essentially zero (t = 0.8), which says the effect is already entirely captured by the daily return — the "far above its open" information is just short-term reversal, not a separate signal. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on the best result by 0.002, so I'll stop here rather than keep fitting the same history.

What I found: the idea is wrong on this history. Coins closing far above their open do not keep rising — the rank IC of the bounded ratio is −0.0277, negative in every sub-period, and once short-term reversal is removed the incremental IC is exactly 0.0000 for the one-day ratio and −0.0074 for the five-day average. So the effect is fully absorbed by the known styles, and I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')).ln().clip(lower=0, upper=3)</factor>

The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: close near the high means buyers dominated that session. I'll measure it as a fraction (close / high) so it's unit-free and comparable across coins, average it over 5 days, and put the minus sign outside because the idea says that's bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0210 (t = -8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0277, 2023 -0.0195, 2024 -0.0191

The sign came out negative and consistently so in every sub-period (−0.028, −0.020, −0.019), which is the expected pattern for a 5-day mean of this close-in-range measure: the 1–5 day reversal style dominates, and the minus sign here is what carried the reversal. Before concluding, I'll try a shorter 3-day window to see whether the reversal contamination is the only thing in the way.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0443
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0194 (t = -7.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0264, 2023 -0.0177, 2024 -0.0174

Three days is a weaker signal (−0.019 vs −0.022), so the 5-day window is the better one and the reversal-contamination reading holds. One more variant is worth a check: a 20-day window, which should be less dominated by the last day's reversal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0490
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0106 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0113, 2023 -0.0061, 2024 -0.0147

The 20-day window is weaker still (−0.011, and the 2023 sub-period is flat), so the 5-day version remains the best of the three. The pattern is clear: the close-in-range measure is actually a reversal signal on this history, and the minus sign here makes it point the wrong way. I'm keeping the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the sign, and I'm handing in the 5-day version, which is the strongest and most stable of the three.

The idea says the high-low range is bearish, so the factor should fall when the range is wide. The range itself is a ratio of price to price, so it is already unit-free and comparable across coins; I'll start with the simplest version, the 5-day average of log(high/low), negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The range version works: +0.0203 incremental IC with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds on this history. Next I'll check whether a longer averaging window (10 days) reduces day-to-day noise in the range measure.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day average is slightly weaker (+0.0186 vs +0.0203), so the shorter window is better and I'll stay with it. Next I'll test a robustness variant: the median of the range over the same 5-day window, since a few wide days should not dominate a mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0552
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0175 (t = 7.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0264, 2023 +0.0136, 2024 +0.0169

The median is clearly worse (+0.0175 vs +0.0203), so the mean is the right aggregation and the longer window is worse — two tests in a row have failed to improve, so I'll stop.

What I found: the idea holds up well on this history. The negated 5-day average of log(high/low) gives an incremental IC of +0.0203 (t = 8.7) with the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so coins whose daily high-low range is wide over the past week do underperform afterwards. The 10-day average (+0.0186) and the 5-day median (+0.0175) both did worse than the 5-day mean, and the longer window also lost to the shorter one, so the signal lives in the recent days rather than in a slow-moving level.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about yesterday's fall: a coin that fell a lot the day before should bounce. So the raw quantity is the one-day return, and the direction is positive (bigger fall → higher factor value). I'll start with the simplest form — the negative of yesterday's return — to see how much of it survives after the known styles are removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain one-day return is fully absorbed by the reversal style (incremental IC 0.0000), so it carries no new information. I'll keep the same direction but measure the fall relative to the coin's own typical daily move — a coin that fell a lot yesterday is unusual for it, which is what the bounce should depend on.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0107
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0006 (t = -0.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0025, 2023 -0.0016, 2024 +0.0013

The z-score form is worse (−0.0006, and the sign flips between periods), so normalizing by the coin's own history doesn't help. A different way to say "fell a lot yesterday" is that the close sits far below the day's high, which is a fall that didn't get absorbed by a single price move. I'll test that form.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0300
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0143 (t = -5.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0263, 2023 -0.0122, 2024 -0.0103

The close-below-high measure is a real signal, but with the sign the idea expects it — it gives −0.0143 incremental IC (t = −5.7), so on this history coins that fell far below their high kept underperforming, not bouncing. That is a real but opposite-to-the-idea effect, and it is consistent across all three periods, so I stop here rather than keep hunting for a form that fits the idea.

What I found: the plain one-day return carries no incremental information at all (0.0000), because it is exactly the short-term reversal style that is already removed. Normalizing it by the coin's own 20-day return (z-score) made it worse (−0.0006). The only form that survives with any signal is the close-below-high version, which is actually negative: coins that fell far below their high went on to do worse, so the bounce idea does not hold here. I keep the direction the idea states and hand in the simplest expression that computes, which is also the one with the highest incremental IC of the three.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says a wide daily high-low range is bearish, so I want the range measured as (high − low) over close — a ratio, so it is comparable across coins regardless of price units — and then negated. I start with the simplest form: the log range averaged over 5 days, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

That reads well: incremental IC +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods, so the direction of the idea holds up. Next I want to check whether the effect is mostly in the quiet days: squaring the range before averaging emphasizes the extreme days, which is a different way to measure "wide range" and may be stronger.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0601
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0200 (t = 8.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0308, 2023 +0.0170, 2024 +0.0176

Squaring gives +0.0200 versus +0.0203 — inside noise, and the extra step is not worth it, so I keep the plain average. One remaining question is whether the 5-day window is doing the work or whether the effect is persistent: I'll stretch the window to 10 days to see if a longer-run range level is stronger.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day version comes in at +0.0186, below the 5-day +0.0203 by more than 0.002, so the shorter window is the better one and I stop here rather than keep tuning the same history.

What I found: measuring the daily range as (high − low) over close and negating it works on this history — coins with a wide range do underperform, with incremental IC +0.0203 (t = 8.7) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, and the sign is consistent in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Emphasizing extreme days (squaring the range) and stretching the window to 10 days both gave back ground, so the effect is a short-horizon one rather than a persistent level, and the plain 5-day average of the log range is the version I hand in.

The idea is about a coin's dollar volume being near its own low end of its recent range, so I'll measure where today's `quote_volume` sits within its own 20-day range (a rank, so it's comparable across coins regardless of price or volume scale), then flip the sign so a low-range position gives a high factor.

rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

Incremental IC of +0.0160 with t = 5.8 and the same sign in all three sub-periods is a decent start — the direction is right, and the level-of-volume position within its own 20-day range is what carries it. Now I'll check whether a longer 60-day window, which should be less noisy, holds up better.

rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

The 60-day window is slightly weaker (+0.0139 vs +0.0160) and 2024 nearly collapses, so the 20-day window is the better one. One more variant worth checking: a robust version of the same quantity, the 20-day median rank, which is less driven by a few huge-volume days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0177
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0016 (t = 0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0111, 2023 +0.0031, 2024 -0.0048

The median version collapses to +0.0016 with t = 0.5 and flips sign in 2024, so the signal is genuinely in the *level* position of volume inside its own range, not in the outlier-resistant shape. That's two tests in a row that failed to beat the 20-day rank by 0.002, so I'll stop here.

What I found: ranking each coin's dollar volume within its own 20-day range and flipping the sign gives an incremental IC of +0.0160 (t = 5.8), with the same sign in 2022H2 (+0.0295), 2023 (+0.0196) and 2024 (+0.0055) — the effect is real but clearly weaker in 2024. Extending the window to 60 days (+0.0139) and replacing the mean with a median (+0.0016) both hurt, so the plain 20-day rank is the version to keep.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about dollar volume: a coin that trades little should do better. The plainest reading is the negative of average dollar volume over a window — `quote_volume` is USDT, so it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit. I'll start with a 20-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The plain level of dollar volume is almost entirely absorbed by the liquidity style — incremental IC is only +0.0011, and 2024 flips slightly negative. So I need to express "trades little" relative to the coin's own normal: a 5-day mean of dollar volume divided by its 60-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

Relative-to-own-normal is much better: +0.0096 incremental, t = 3.3, and all three periods point the same way (2024 is weak but still positive). Next I'll check whether a longer baseline (120 days) smooths the same quantity better, since "trades little" is a persistent trait rather than a 60-day one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0394
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0090 (t = 3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0121, 2023 +0.0123, 2024 +0.0040

The 120-day baseline gives +0.0090, only 0.0006 better than the 60-day one — inside noise, and it is the second test in a row that failed to beat the best by 0.002, so I stop here.

What I found: the level of dollar volume is mostly the liquidity style — its incremental IC is only +0.0011, and 2024 even turns slightly negative. Measuring "trades little" against the coin's own 60-day norm does carry information beyond that: +0.0096 incremental (t = 3.3), positive in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014). The effect is real but weak in 2024, so the idea looks right in direction but not strong on this history. The 60-day baseline was the best of the three, so I hand that in.

The idea is about the day's close relative to its own open: a coin that closes far above its open should keep rising. That is a ratio, so it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit. I'll start with the simplest version — the daily close-to-open ratio, averaged over 5 days — to see how much of it survives after the known styles are removed.

rank IC: -0.0400
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0003 (t = -1.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0010, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 -0.0004

The plain 5-day average is essentially flat: incremental IC −0.0003, and the raw rank IC is −0.040, so on this history coins closing far above open actually did slightly worse. Before concluding, I'll check whether the effect is concentrated in a few extreme days — a 20-day median of the same ratio — to see if the signal lives in the outliers rather than in the average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0126
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0020 (t = -0.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0016, 2023 -0.0036, 2024 -0.0021

The 20-day median is also essentially flat (−0.0020, t = −0.7), so the effect is not concentrated in the extremes — it is genuinely weak, and the raw rank IC is the opposite sign to the idea. One more form is worth trying: the same close-to-open gap measured against the coin's own typical daily move, which keeps the same "far above open" idea but is bounded and less driven by a single print.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0191
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0001 (t = 0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0008, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0008

That is the third form in a row that lands between −0.002 and +0.001 with t-values under 1, so the window is not the problem. I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the same quantity.

What I found: measuring the close-to-open gap as a ratio (close/open minus one) gives a raw rank IC of −0.040 and an incremental IC of −0.0003, meaning coins closing far above their open went on to underperform slightly on this history — the opposite of the idea, and the sign does not flip across periods. The 20-day median and the same gap divided by its own 20-day standard deviation both came in at −0.0020 and +0.0001, so the effect is real in the raw data but entirely absorbed by the known styles; it is not a signal worth keeping, and I keep the idea's direction rather than flipping it to chase the score.

The idea says a recent high in dollar volume is bearish, so the factor should be low when volume has just jumped. I'll measure the ratio of a short-window mean dollar volume to a long-window mean (a "recent high"), and put a minus sign on the outside so that the factor falls when volume spikes.

rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

The 5-vs-60 window gives +0.0096 incremental with t = 3.3 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is nearly flat. Since the idea stresses the *recent* high, I'll try a shorter short window (3 days) to see whether the spike is more informative than the 5-day mean.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0215, 2023 +0.0157, 2024 +0.0112

The 3-day vs 20-day window jumps to +0.0151 (t = 5.5) with all three periods positive, so the recent-high reading is the right one. Next I'll check whether the spike is better captured by a single day's volume against its own 20-day average, which is the literal "just hit a recent high" reading.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0252, 2023 +0.0142, 2024 +0.0052

The single-day version lands at +0.0128, below the +0.0151 of the 3-day mean, so averaging the volume over a few days is better than a single day. That is one test short of the 5, so I'll stop here and submit the best tested form.

What I found: a recent dollar-volume spike does predict underperformance, and the effect is strongest when the spike is measured over the past few days against a longer baseline (3-day mean over 20 days, +0.0151, t = 5.5, positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024). Measuring the spike as a single day's volume against its own 20-day average (+0.0128) or as a 5-day mean over a 60-day baseline (+0.0096) is both weaker, and 2024 is nearly flat in the first case. The sign is kept as the idea states: coins with just-hit volume get a low factor value.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain daily return is entirely absorbed by the reversal style — incremental IC is 0.0000, and its rank IC is negative, so on this history close-above-open has been followed by weakness. Before concluding, I'll test a robust form of the same quantity: the gap measured as a log difference, which keeps the same direction but shrinks big-gap days and is less like a raw return.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The log form is also exactly 0.0000 incremental — the raw return is just a return, and the reversal style eats it whole. So the level of the gap carries no independent information. The idea's word "tend" implies a persistent habit rather than a single day, so I'll test the gap over a few days, which is still a return-difference quantity but built from a window.

rank IC: -0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0001 (t = 0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 -0.0001

The 5-day average of the gap is still exactly 0.0000 incremental, so averaging the gap doesn't rescue anything — it's the same quantity, and the reversal style has already taken it. One last form worth checking: the gap as a rank within the coin's own recent history, which is a different shape of the same "closing far above its open" quantity and is not a return difference.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0140
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0015 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0014, 2023 -0.0006, 2024 -0.0039

The rank form is also 0.0015 incremental — still nothing, and with the sign flipping between periods. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on the best by 0.002, so I stop here.

Its raw rank IC is slightly negative (−0.0175), meaning coins that closed far above their open did slightly *worse* the next day on this history, which is the opposite of the idea. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping the sign to chase the score; the honest reading is that this idea does not hold on 2022–2024 USDT perpetuals.
